```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

```{r setup}
library(chainlink)
```

Chain-linked volume measures are not additive, so that the contribution of a
component to the growth of the total cannot be read from the growth of the
components. `chain_contrib()` computes exact contributions: they add up to the
growth of the total (up to the inconsistencies of the data, see below).

# Principle

Let `x` be the chain volume measure (in monetary terms) of a component and `z`
the one of the total. Within a year `y`, the chain volume measure of the total is
exactly the sum of the chain volume measures of the components, valued at the
relative prices `rho` of the previous year (`y - 1`):

```
z[t] = sum over the components i of rho[i, y - 1] * x[i, t]
```

* annual overlap (`method = "ao"`): `rho[i, y]` is the price of the component `i`
  relative to the price of the total in year `y`, with annual sums
  `(cp[i, y] / x[i, y]) / (cp[z, y] / z[y])`;
* one-quarter overlap (`method = "oqo"`): `rho[i, y]` is the same ratio computed
  on the overlap period (the last quarter, or the last month, of year `y`).

The contribution of the component `i` to the growth between a period `s` and a
period `t` (previous period, same period of the previous year, or previous year) is

```
100 * [ (x[t] - x[s]) * rho[y(t) - 1] / z[s]
      + (x[s] / z[s] - a[y(t) - 1]) * (rho[y(t) - 1] - rho[y(s) - 1]) ]
```

where `a[y]` is the share of the component in the total (annual share for the annual
overlap, share of the overlap period for the one-quarter overlap). The second term
is zero if `s` and `t` are in the same year. For the annual overlap and the growth
over the previous period, this is the formula of the example 8.9 of the manual.
The formula for the one-quarter overlap, and for the growth over the same period of
the previous year, derive from the same decomposition: they add up to the growth of the
total exactly.

The breakdown between the components is not unique, only its sum is: the second
term (revaluation due to the change of relative prices) is allocated as in the
manual.

# Example

`chain_laspeyres()` computes the chain volume measures of the components and of
their total (last column):

```{r}
x <- chain_laspeyres(data8.2cp, data8.2ep, method = "ao", base_year = 2010,
					 output = "measure")
round(x, 3)
```

Contributions to the growth over the previous quarter (`type = "period"`, the
default). `extra` adds the growth of the total and the residual (growth of the
total minus the sum of the contributions):

```{r}
chain_contrib(x, data8.2cp, method = "ao", extra = c("total", "residual")) |>
	round(3)
```

Contributions to the growth over the same quarter of the previous year:

```{r}
chain_contrib(x, data8.2cp, method = "ao", type = "yoy", extra = "total") |>
	round(3)
```

Contributions to the growth of the annual sums:

```{r}
chain_contrib(x, data8.2cp, method = "ao", type = "annual", extra = "total") |>
	round(3)
```

# One-quarter overlap

```{r}
x_oqo <- chain_laspeyres(data8.2cp, data8.2ep, method = "oqo", base_year = 2010,
						 output = "measure")
chain_contrib(x_oqo, data8.2cp, method = "oqo", type = "period", pi = data8.2ep,
			  extra = c("total", "residual")) |>
	round(3)
```

The overlap quarter is valued at the average prices of the year, as in the manual
(`cp_pi2cy()`): `chain_contrib()` needs the price indices `pi` to do so (or `cp`
already valued at these prices). With the one-quarter overlap technique, the
contributions to the annual growth are only available from the second year (the
annual sum of the base year is not defined).

# Correspondence with the manual

* annual overlap: `type = "period"` and `type = "annual"` are the equations (29)
  (quarters 2 to 4 and annual data) and (30) (first quarter) of the paragraphs
  8.86-8.87, and `type = "yoy"` is the equation (31) of the paragraph 8.88. The
  example 8.9 is reproduced by the tests of the package;
* one-quarter overlap: the manual (footnote 35) applies the same formulas with the
  annual deflators, but the contributions are then not exactly additive. The
  package provides this variant with `method = "ao"` applied to the one-quarter
  overlap measures, and an exactly additive version with `method = "oqo"`:

```{r oqo-manual}
x_oqo <- chain_laspeyres(data8.2cp, data8.2ep, method = "oqo", base_year = 2010,
						 output = "measure")
# Formulas of the manual (annual deflators)
chain_contrib(x_oqo, data8.2cp, method = "ao", extra = "residual") |> round(4)
# Deflators of the overlap period (valued at the average prices of the year)
chain_contrib(x_oqo, data8.2cp, method = "oqo", pi = data8.2ep,
			  extra = "residual") |> round(4)
```

* a variable that can be negative, zero or positive (changes in inventories) is
  treated residually (paragraph 8.90): its contribution is the difference between
  the contribution of the aggregate that includes it and the contributions of the
  other components.

# Quarterly Fisher indices

The paragraph 8.89 gives the contributions to the percent change of a quarterly
Fisher index. `fisher_contrib()` takes the current prices of all the components and
their price indices over the previous quarter (`pi_py2pp()` converts price
indices over the previous year):

```{r fisher}
ep8.4 <- pi_py2pp(data8.2ep)
fisher_contrib(data8.2cp, ep8.4, extra = c("total", "residual")) |> round(3)
```

This is the equation (32) of the manual. The decomposition is exact: the residual
is zero up to numerical errors. As printed in the manual, the equation has the
ratio `z[t-1] / z[t]` in the first term and `x[t-1] * p[t-1] / p[t]` in the second
one; with these ratios, the contributions do not add up to the percent change.
The version implemented uses `z[t] / z[t-1]` and `x[t-1] * p[t] / p[t-1]`
(consistent with the price relative of the denominator). The
adjustments that some countries add to the quarterly contributions (benchmarking
of the quarterly indices, annual rates) are not done.

# Non-additivity and residual

Two different things must not be mixed up:

* the chain volume measures are not additive: the chain measure of the total is not
  the sum of the chain measures of the components (`chain_discrepancy()`). It is zero
  in the base year and, with the annual overlap, in the year after;
* the contributions take this into account and add up to the growth of the total. The
  residual (`extra = "residual"`) is therefore zero if the data are fully
  consistent, i.e. if the annual price indices are exactly those of the quarterly
  data. In the example of the manual, they are not (the residual is small, below
  0.001 percentage point).

```{r}
chain_discrepancy(x) |> round(3)
chain_discrepancy(x, relative = TRUE) |> round(3)
```

# Monthly data

The functions use the frequency of the series. As an illustration, each quarter of the
data of the example is spread over three months (the contributions are then
non-zero only for the first month of each quarter, when the quarter changes):

```{r}
spread <- function(a, scale = 1) {
	m <- as.matrix(a)
	res <- ts(m[rep(seq_len(nrow(m)), each = 3), , drop = FALSE] * scale,
			  start = c(start(a)[1], 1), frequency = 12)
	colnames(res) <- colnames(a)
	res
}
cp_m <- spread(data8.2cp, 1 / 3)
pi_m <- spread(data8.2ep)
x_m <- chain_laspeyres(cp_m, pi_m, method = "ao", base_year = 2010,
					   output = "measure")
chain_contrib(x_m, cp_m, method = "ao") |>
	window(start = c(2011, 1), end = c(2011, 8)) |>
	round(3)
```

# Variables that change sign

Growth rates and chain volume measures are meaningless for a variable that can be
negative, zero or positive, such as changes in inventories (paragraph 8.56 of the
manual). Two solutions:

* contributions are calculated residually (paragraph 8.90): the contribution of
  the variable is the difference between the contribution of the aggregate that
  includes it and the contributions of the other components;
* a pseudo chain volume series is derived (paragraphs 8.57-8.58): the variable is
  written as the difference of two series that only take positive values (closing
  minus opening inventories, exports minus imports), each of them is chain-linked
  separately, and the chain volume series is their difference. `chain_pseudo()`
  does it, from the current prices and the price indices of the two series
  (the two products of the example below only stand in for them):

```{r pseudo}
chain_pseudo(data8.2cp[, "A"], data8.2ep[, "A"],
			 data8.2cp[, "B"], data8.2ep[, "B"], base_year = 2010) |> round(1)
```

# Change of the reference year

`chain_rebase()` changes the reference year of an index (the average of the new
year is 100) or of a measure (the annual sum of the new year is its annual current
prices). The growth rates are unchanged.

```{r}
chain_laspeyres(data8.2cp, data8.2ep, base_year = 2010) |>
	chain_rebase(base_year = 2012) |>
	round(2)
```
